model_annotation: Figure 3(a) presents a line plot illustrating the training loss curves for different methods during training from scratch, with the vertical axis labeled “Loss” and the horizontal axis labeled “Training steps (×10⁶)”, ranging from 0 to 1.4 in increments of 0.2. The plot compares five methods: Vanilla (black solid line with circle markers), StrmLM (n=256) (red dashed line with square markers), SepLM (n=256) (blue dash-dot line with diamond markers), SepLM (n=64) (green dotted line with triangle markers), and SepLM (n=64,H/T) (purple solid line with inverted triangle markers). All curves begin near a loss value of 1.1 at 0 training steps and generally decline as training steps increase. The Vanilla method starts with the highest loss and decreases steadily to approximately 0.75 at 1.4×10⁶ steps. StrmLM (n=256) begins slightly lower than Vanilla and declines to about 0.85. SepLM (n=256) starts at roughly 0.95 and decreases to approximately 0.78. SepLM (n=64) begins near 0.9 and drops to around 0.76. SepLM (n=64,H/T) starts at approximately 0.92 and declines to about 0.77. The legend is embedded within the plot area, identifying each line by method name and parameter configuration.
